title: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin
summary: Ipamorelin and sermorelin are both discussed for raising growth hormone, but they are different classes of drug acting on different receptors. Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of the body's own growth-hormone-releasing hormone, GHRH; it was approved in the United States in 1997 for children with growth hormone deficiency and withdrawn from the market in 2008 for commercial rather than safety reasons. Ipamorelin is a synthetic ghrelin-receptor agonist that was never approved. No study has compared them head to head. Sermorelin's human record is larger and older; ipamorelin's is two trials. The two are often combined rather than chosen between, on the physiology that GHRH and ghrelin signals amplify each other.

seo.title: Ipamorelin vs Sermorelin: Two Receptors, One Hormone
seo.description: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin: different receptors, a once-approved medicine against a never-approved one, half-lives, human evidence, and no direct comparison.

faq.question: Which is better, ipamorelin or sermorelin?
faq.answer: The evidence cannot say. They act on different receptors, neither has a trial for the uses adults pursue, and no study compares them.

faq.question: Is sermorelin FDA approved?
faq.answer: It was, from 1997 for children with growth hormone deficiency, and was withdrawn in 2008 for commercial reasons. It is not currently an approved product, though it has been available through compounding.

faq.question: Is ipamorelin FDA approved?
faq.answer: No. It failed a phase 2 trial and was never approved; it sits in Category 2 of the FDA's interim compounding list.

faq.question: Can ipamorelin and sermorelin be taken together?
faq.answer: They are combined in communities on the reasoning that a GHRH signal and a ghrelin signal amplify each other. No trial has tested the pair.

faq.question: Which has the longer half-life?
faq.answer: Ipamorelin, at about two hours in the human pharmacokinetic study, against roughly ten to twenty minutes for sermorelin.

faq.question: Are they banned in sport?
faq.answer: Both, under WADA S2, at all times.

open_questions: No study compares the two for any outcome.
Sermorelin's adult wellness use has no trial support despite its paediatric approval history.
Neither compound has been tested for body composition, sleep or recovery in healthy adults.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin in two minutes
guide.html:
Different receptors. Sermorelin is a GHRH analogue: it acts where the hypothalamus's own releasing hormone acts. Ipamorelin acts on the ghrelin receptor. Both end in the pituitary releasing growth hormone, which is why they are compared, and why they are also combined.

Different histories. Sermorelin (Geref) was an approved paediatric medicine from 1997 until its manufacturer withdrew it in 2008; it has since been widely available through US compounding pharmacies. Ipamorelin was developed by Novo Nordisk, failed a phase 2 trial for post-surgical gut recovery, and was never approved.

Evidence. Sermorelin has a real clinical record in children with growth hormone deficiency and diagnostic use in adults; its adult "anti-ageing" use has no trial support. Ipamorelin has a pharmacokinetic study and one failed trial. Neither has a trial for body composition, sleep or recovery in healthy adults.

Head to head. Nothing. No indexed study compares them.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin: the human studies on record
guide.lede: What each compound has actually been tested for in people.
guide.html:
Ipamorelin. Two human studies. In 1999, healthy men given ipamorelin released growth hormone at every dose tested, and it left the blood with a half-life of about 2 hours.{{cite:pmid-10496658}} In 2014, a trial in 114 patients recovering from bowel surgery found no significant difference from placebo on its main or secondary recovery measures.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} That failed trial ended its clinical development.

Sermorelin. A longer record, mostly in children. In a 1996 study of 110 children with growth hormone deficiency given daily injections, average growth rose from 4.1 cm a year to 8.0 and 7.2 cm a year at 6 and 12 months, with no control group.{{cite:pmid-8772599}} In older adults, a 1997 placebo-controlled study of a modified form of sermorelin raised overnight growth hormone levels in both women and men.{{cite:pmid-9141536}} No trial on record tests either compound for the body-composition, sleep or recovery uses adults pursue.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin side effects
guide.lede: What the two records hold, which is very little.
guide.html:
The 2014 ipamorelin trial tracked safety through side effects and laboratory tests, but its published abstract gives no side-effect results.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} The sermorelin record holds no side-effect finding from a source this site can cite. Neither absence means the compound has no side effects. It means the studies on record did not report them in a form that can be cited here.

The full records are on the ipamorelin and sermorelin pages.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin dosage in the studies
guide.lede: Doses studies administered, reported as published. None is a suggestion.
guide.html:
Ipamorelin. The one treatment trial gave 0.03 mg/kg by infusion into a vein twice daily, from the day after surgery until day 7 or discharge.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} That is a hospital regimen, not how ipamorelin circulates outside trials.

Sermorelin. Children with growth hormone deficiency were given 30 µg/kg once daily under the skin for 12 to 24 months.{{cite:pmid-7735367}} Older adults in the 1997 study injected 10 µg/kg of a modified sermorelin nightly for 16 weeks.{{cite:pmid-9141536}} Diagnostic studies used single injections into a vein, as low as 0.05 and 0.15 µg/kg.{{cite:pmid-10754477}}

The circulating figures are in the comparison table above as commonly reported use. None has been tested in a trial for the uses it is reported for.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs sermorelin cycle length: how long studies gave each one
guide.lede: Treatment periods on record, not recommended courses.
guide.html: Ipamorelin's longest human course is the bowel-surgery trial: twice-daily infusions for up to 7 days.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} Sermorelin was given for 12 months in the 1996 children's study{{cite:pmid-8772599}} and for 12 to 24 months in another{{cite:pmid-7735367}}; the 1997 study in older adults gave 16 weeks of the modified form after 4 weeks of placebo.{{cite:pmid-9141536}} Every compound's study durations are on the peptide cycle length page.

guide.heading: Who should avoid ipamorelin or sermorelin?
guide.lede: No trial or current label on record defines it for either.
guide.html: Neither record holds exclusion criteria from a trial or a current approved label that this page can cite, so there is no evidence-based list of who should avoid them. That is an absence of evidence, not a sign that they suit everyone. Two facts on record still apply: both are named under section S2 of the WADA Prohibited List, prohibited at all times, so athletes subject to testing are covered by that rule; and ipamorelin has appeared in the FDA's Category 2 for compounding, the category for substances with significant safety concerns. What each record does hold is on the ipamorelin and sermorelin pages.

guide.heading: How the two are discussed as choices
guide.html: The community framing is that sermorelin is the "legal" or "prescribable" option because of its approval history and compounding availability, while ipamorelin is the "cleaner" option because of its reported selectivity for growth hormone over cortisol and prolactin. Both framings have something behind them and neither is an efficacy claim: sermorelin's approval was for children who lack the hormone, and ipamorelin's selectivity was shown in animals and healthy volunteers. Neither compound has been tested for the outcomes adults use them for. Because they act on different receptors, they are more often combined than chosen between, which is the same logic as the CJC-1295 and ipamorelin blend with a shorter-acting GHRH analogue. The tesamorelin and ipamorelin stack follows the same pattern with an approved GHRH analogue.
